text:
maya: heads-up — we're seeing a latency spike for inference jobs in us-east-1a, a few pods OOMing and some jobs throwing Xid 41/12 intermittently
ops-bot: alert: nvlink-aer-rate increase detected on rack-17 (threshold exceeded)
ryan: ugh, Xid 41 usually points to ECC/firmware flake or pcie aerr. Maya, can you paste the kernel logs from one of the affected nodes?
maya: paste coming — i grabbed dmesg + nvidia logs from node-17-04
maya: ```
[ 12345.678901] pcieport 0000:65:00.0: AER: Corrected error received: device 65:00
[ 12345.678905] nvidia: Xid (PCIe: 41, engine 0040) 00bbbbbb
[ 12345.679010] nvlink0: link 1 flapping, retrain attempt 3
[ 12345.679120] pcieport 0000:65:00.0: PCIe Bus Error: severity=Corrected, type=Physical Layer, id=00a0
```
anika: nvlink flaps + AER corrected errors — suggests intermittent signal integrity issue. Could be cabling/riser or BIOS settings. How many nodes impacted?
maya: so far 3 nodes in rack-17 (17-02, 17-04, 17-07). All are delivering occasional frame errors and Xid 41. Not every job, but frequency up in past 2 hours.
leo: checking telemetry: thermal still OK, ECC error counters ramping on those cards — not showing permanent memory errors yet, mostly recovered ECC and retry counts.
ryan: good — not a hard ECC fail. Plan: take 17-04 out of service, repro traffic to other nodes, see if issue follows card or slot. Can someone run a quick nvlink diag on 17-04 and 17-02?
manual: (human) i will run now
maya: running: `sudo nvidia-smi -q -d MEMORY,PCI,PERFORMANCE` — output: PCIe Tx CRC errors incrementing on GPU A of 17-04
anika: tx CRC errors on one side consistent with signal/cable or riser intermittency. If we drain and swap cards between 17-04 and 17-02 we can determine whether it's slot or card. Time to RMA if card follows.
sre-oncall: we need to schedule draining carefully — us-east-1a is at 78% GPU capacity for hosted inference; draining 3 nodes will push some customers into queued/backoff. Consider routing fallback to us-east-1b for latency-sensitive tenants.
ryan: agree. I'll open a short maintenance window pinned to non-peak: start in 20m, duration 45m. Can we do a temporary regional failover? Ops, can we ramp up spare capacity in 1b?
ops-bot: autoscale: launched 4 spare GPU instances in us-east-1b (on-demand), estimated cost delta ~$420/day.
leo: ok that covers capacity for the drain window. Ops-bot, please tag these instances as "nvlink-failover-1769554321"
ops-bot: done — instances tagged.
ryan: drain command: `rkctl drain-node node-17-04 --grace-period 600` — will evict training and inference pods. Maya, once drained, swap GPU A from 17-04 into 17-02 physically (schedule with hw team) or attempt a hot-swap?
maya: hw team asked to confirm: we prefer to power-cycle and reseat first, then swap if reoccurs. I'll coordinate.
anika: if reseat fixes it, likely riser/cable. If errors move with card -> RMA. Also log current firmware versions — I've seen mismatch cause nvlink retrain loops.
maya: firmware on 17-04 GPU A: 52.3.9, 17-02 GPU A: 52.3.9 — matching.
sre-oncall: please add temporary routing rule to prefer us-east-1b for new sessions for tier-enterprise customers to preserve SLOs. We'll keep hosted API rate limiters unchanged but shift routing policy.\ryan: created rollout: routing policy "prefer-1b" for enterprise via config manager. Canary to 5% then 50% in 10m.
infra-bot: change approved by oncall. Canary started: 5% traffic -> us-east-1b.
maya: node-17-04 drained, evicted pods, powering down for reseat now.
maya: reseat done, powering up. Monitoring logs.
maya: after reseat — still seeing occasional nvlink retrain and Xid 41 on same GPU A
leo: errors continuing after reseat — do the errors follow the card if we swap it?
maya: swapping cards scheduled in 30m with hw tech (safety + documentation).
ryan: interim: mark GPUs in node metadata as "suspect-nvlink" so scheduler avoids them for latency-sensitive queues.
ops-bot: metadata updated for node-17-02 and node-17-04: label applied suspect:nvlink-1769554321
anika: when swap happens, collect `nvidia-bug-report.sh --allow-temp-files` and send to HW + nv support; include system dmesg and the pcie aerr counters.
leo: agreed. Also export kernel oops logs and lower-level PCIe PHY counters from BMC if available.
sre-oncall: we've kept SLOs stable via 1b failover; cost hit minimal for now. Please file a postmortem if we end up RMAing more than 1 card.
ryan: created ticket INFRA-4921 with logs, diagnostic steps, and action items (drain, reseat, swap, RMA if card follows). Assigning to hw-team and eng-infra.
ops-bot: ticket INFRA-4921 created and linked to this thread.
maya: thanks — will update after swap. For now all monitoring dashboards show reduced user impact.
anika: if we see similar pattern across racks, we should consider running a batch check on riser firmware and backplane connectors across east-1 region.
ryan: noted. Let's reconvene in 1 hour or earlier if swap shows regression. :thumbsup:
infra-bot: audit log: node-17-04 drained by ryan at 1769554420; reseat performed at 1769554530; card swap scheduled at 1769556320.
